title.narrative: Increased institutional capacity of employer and business membership organizations to be strong, independent and representative

description.narrative: The following are the major global deliverables and activities of the ILO in this policy area. (1) Development of global knowledge products that can be customized to local contexts and that support EBMOs’ policy agenda and service delivery, with special attention to themes that promote the mutual interests of business and society, such as environmental, social and governance issues, crisis and resilience, and violence and harassment at work. (2) Resources to enhance the representativeness of EBMOs by designing models to attract micro, small and medium-sized enterprises and integrating new forms of business or sectors, and methods of building alliances with like-minded partners and with informal economic actors to achieve common objectives. (3) Tools to strengthen gender diversity and inclusion in EBMOs’ governance structures and to preserve their institutional and operational independence. (4) As a follow-up to the Centenary Declaration, production of global research on the role of employers in upholding social justice and democracy by advocating for the rule of law and good governance at national and international levels, and their role in fostering inclusive growth and sustainable development. (5) Entry points for ILO engagement with the private sector, including through initiatives such as the ILO Global Business Network on Forced Labour.
